title: 2026 Maine Gubernatorial Election
description: The 2026 Maine gubernatorial election on November 3, 2026, is an open-seat race to succeed term-limited Democratic Governor Janet Mills in a state that has not elected consecutive governors from the same party since 1952. Primary elections on June 9 used ranked-choice voting; after five days of tabulation, former State House Speaker Hannah Pingree clinched the Democratic nomination by defeating former Maine CDC Director Nirav Shah 56%-44% in the final round, while attorney and former federal official Bobby Charles secured the Republican nomination after six rounds of tabulation. State Senator Rick Bennett qualified as an independent candidate, setting up a three-way general election contest that will be decided by plurality vote, not ranked-choice voting. Maine has voted Democratic in every presidential election since 1992 and is considered moderately blue, yet a Republican has not won a majority in a gubernatorial race since 1962, keeping the race highly competitive.

candidates.name: Hannah Pingree
candidates.summary: Hannah Pingree is the Democratic nominee for governor after winning a five-way ranked-choice primary on June 19, 2026. She served as Speaker of the Maine House of Representatives from 2008 to 2010 and most recently as director of Governor Janet Mills' Office of Policy Innovation and the Future. Her campaign emphasizes affordable housing, clean energy, holding utilities accountable, and making the tax code more progressive with a millionaire's tax and increased Homestead Exemption.

Economy.stance: Pingree’s economic plan centers on affordability to raise wages and lower living costs by investing $100 million per year in affordable housing. It also includes measures to lower energy and health-care costs, expand access to childcare, and grow wages through workforce training and targeted rural economic development.

candidates.summary: Robert "Bobby" Charles is the Republican nominee for governor after winning an eight-way ranked-choice primary on June 19, 2026. An attorney and Leeds resident, he served as Assistant Secretary of State for International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs under President George W. Charles has run a Trump-style campaign emphasizing border security, cutting taxes and regulation, and has been a vocal opponent of ranked-choice voting.

candidates.name: Rick Bennett
candidates.summary: Rick Bennett is an independent candidate for governor, a State Senator representing District 18, and former chair of the Maine Republican Party. He qualified for the general election ballot by submitting petition signatures, setting up a three-way contest against Democratic nominee Hannah Pingree and Republican nominee Bobby Charles. Bennett has positioned himself as a centrist alternative focused on energy affordability, childcare, and health care cost reduction.

Economy.stance: Rick Bennett supports a four-part energy affordability plan to boost Maine's economy by lowering delivery costs and reducing energy costs for heritage industries; the plan also includes weatherizing homes with a $30 million investment and creating a Maine Generation Authority to stabilize supply costs and keep renewable benefits in-state.

forecast.rationale: With no public polling available, this forecast relies on non-polling fundamentals only. Maine is a moderately Democratic-leaning state at the presidential level and Democrats hold the governorship, which gives Democratic nominee Hannah Pingree a narrow structural edge in an open-seat race. However, Maine has a long history of competitive gubernatorial elections, the state has not elected consecutive governors from the same party since 1952, and this is a three-way plurality contest with independent Rick Bennett on the ballot, all of which increase uncertainty and create a plausible Republican path for Bobby Charles. Pingree appears to be the strongest-positioned candidate on paper given Democratic baseline strength and fundraising, but the lack of polling and the volatility of a three-candidate race keep the contest close.
